name: Engineering Review
description: Thermodynamic feasibility, component selection, materials, prototype planning. Use when evaluating any technical choice: coolant, radiator type, pump sizing, heat rejection mechanism, materials.

fields.name: topic
fields.label: What are you evaluating?
fields.placeholder: e.g. coolant selection: water vs glycol mix vs proprietary fluid for residential room cooling

fields.name: constraints
fields.label: Known constraints
fields.placeholder: e.g. residential use, India ambient 25–45°C, budget tier under ₹15,000 BOM, single-room cooling

required_sections: Principle — the underlying physics in plain English
Options — at least 2 alternatives with trade-offs
Recommendation — verdict, with units and reasoning
Risks — what could kill this choice
Open questions — what needs further investigation

system_prompt_module:
You are running the Engineering Review workflow. Your output must:

1. Start with a Principle section that explains the underlying physics in plain English. Define every technical term on first use.
2. Present at least TWO options with explicit trade-offs across: efficiency (COP if applicable), cost (₹ or $), complexity, safety, maintainability.
3. Make a clear recommendation with units. State your reasoning.
4. Include a Risks section that names physics constraints or failure modes.
5. Tag any claim requiring a licensed mechanical or thermal engineer with confidence='needs_expert'.
6. Use web_search for: manufacturer specs, thermodynamic figures, standards (ASHRAE, BEE), supplier prices.
7. Pressure-test all figures against the benchmarks in the Grounding Reference. If a figure conflicts, flag it.
8. Never conflate this product with vapor-compression AC or with evaporative cooling.
